tracks.narration: Four wires want to share one output line — how do we pick which one talks?
A four to one multiplexer: four data inputs on the left, two select bits at the bottom, and a single output on the right.
Walk the select bits from zero zero up to one one. Whichever input is addressed lights up, and its signal walks through the block to the output.
In Boolean form, Y is the OR of four AND terms: each data line ANDed with the decoded address that selects it.
A multiplexer is a programmable switch — and chaining them lets one address space pick from many more lines.
